candidate.key_mechanism: Entropy and n-gram statistics measure the predictability of symbol sequences.
candidate.name: Shannon information theory
candidate.problem_solved: Quantified information and prediction, founding statistical language modeling.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Foundation of information theory and LM evaluation.

candidate.key_mechanism: Conditional probabilities over word histories with smoothing and backoff.
candidate.name: N-gram language models
candidate.problem_solved: Predicted words from fixed-order Markov statistics for speech recognition.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Standard LM technology for three decades.

candidate.name: TRPO (trust region policy optimization)
candidate.causal_claim: PPO's direct predecessor - PPO is explicitly 'a first-order approximation of TRPO' that keeps its stability without second-order machinery.
candidate.definition: Algorithm (Schulman et al., 2015): policy updates constrained to a trust region via a KL bound, with monotonic-improvement guarantees.
candidate.source_title: Trust Region Policy Optimization

candidate.name: REINFORCE (Williams)
candidate.causal_claim: The founding policy-gradient method; the entire lineage PPO belongs to descends from it.
candidate.definition: Algorithm (Williams, 1992): gradient ascent on expected reward using sampled returns - the original policy-gradient estimator.
candidate.source_title: Simple statistical gradient-following algorithms for connectionist reinforcement learning

candidate.name: Policy gradient theorem (Sutton et al.)
candidate.causal_claim: The mathematical foundation that makes policy-gradient methods (REINFORCE, actor-critic, TRPO, PPO) well-defined.
candidate.definition: Theorem (Sutton, McAllester, Singh & Mansour, 2000): the gradient of expected return can be written without differentiating the state distribution.
candidate.source_title: Policy Gradient Methods for Reinforcement Learning with Function Approximation

candidate.name: Actor-critic methods (Konda & Tsitsiklis)
candidate.causal_claim: The variance-reduction architecture inside TRPO/PPO practice - but consumed packaged in those methods, not directly.
candidate.definition: Framework (Konda & Tsitsiklis, 2000-2003): a critic estimates values to reduce the variance of an actor's policy-gradient updates.
candidate.source_title: Actor-Critic Algorithms

candidate.name: Natural policy gradient (Kakade)
candidate.causal_claim: The intellectual parent of trust-region methods; its channel into PPO runs through TRPO.
candidate.definition: Method (Kakade, 2002): follow the gradient in the Fisher-information metric rather than raw parameter space.
candidate.source_title: A Natural Policy Gradient

candidate.name: Conservative policy iteration (Kakade & Langford)
candidate.causal_claim: An early improvement-guarantee method whose lineage runs into TRPO.
candidate.definition: Algorithm (Kakade & Langford, 2002): conservative mixture updates with approximate monotonic improvement guarantees.
candidate.source_title: Approximately Optimal Approximate Reinforcement Learning

candidate.name: Generalized advantage estimation (GAE)
candidate.causal_claim: PPO's companion estimator - the advantage signal PPO's clipped objective consumes in standard implementations (and in all RLHF codebases).
candidate.definition: Estimator (Schulman et al., 2016): exponentially-weighted advantage estimates trading bias against variance via a lambda parameter.
candidate.source_title: High-Dimensional Continuous Control Using Generalized Advantage Estimation

candidate.name: Deep Q-Network (DQN)
candidate.causal_claim: A parallel value-based lineage; PPO's policy-gradient family does not consume it.
candidate.definition: System (Mnih et al., 2015): value-based deep RL with experience replay and target networks, reaching human-level Atari play.
candidate.source_title: Human-level control through deep reinforcement learning

candidate.name: A3C asynchronous actor-critic
candidate.causal_claim: A contemporary baseline PPO was compared against, not an input to it.
candidate.definition: Method (Mnih et al., 2016): asynchronous parallel actor-learners for actor-critic RL.
candidate.source_title: Asynchronous Methods for Deep Reinforcement Learning

candidate.name: OpenAI Gym
candidate.causal_claim: Infrastructure the RL community used, but not a causal input to PPO's algorithm.
candidate.definition: Toolkit (Brockman et al., 2016): standardized RL environments and evaluation protocol.
candidate.source_title: OpenAI Gym

candidate.name: Importance sampling for off-policy evaluation (Precup et al.)
candidate.causal_claim: PPO's probability-ratio objective is importance-sampling-flavored, but the consumed formulation arrives via TRPO's surrogate objective.
candidate.definition: Technique (Precup, Sutton & Dasgupta, 2000): reweight trajectories from a behavior policy to evaluate a target policy.
candidate.source_title: Eligibility Traces for Off-Policy Policy Evaluation

candidate.name: DDPG (deep deterministic policy gradient)
candidate.causal_claim: A parallel off-policy lineage; not consumed by PPO.

candidate.source_title: Continuous control with deep reinforcement learning

candidate.name: Transformer architecture
candidate.causal_claim: GPT-2 is a stack of Transformer decoder blocks; the architecture reaches it as part of the GPT-1 recipe it inherited and scaled.
candidate.definition: Architecture (Vaswani et al., 2017) replacing recurrence with self-attention; the substrate of all modern LLMs.
candidate.source_title: Attention Is All You Need

candidate.name: ULMFiT
candidate.lens: immediate prior state of the art
candidate.causal_claim: ULMFiT proved pretrain-then-fine-tune for NLP months before GPT-1, defining the transfer paradigm GPT-2's zero-shot move reacted against and extended.
candidate.definition: Method (Howard & Ruder, 2018): LM pretraining, LM fine-tuning, classifier fine-tuning with discriminative rates and gradual unfreezing, large gains on text classification.
candidate.source_title: Universal Language Model Fine-tuning for Text Classification

candidate.name: ELMo
candidate.lens: immediate prior state of the art
candidate.causal_claim: ELMo showed contextualized representations from a pretrained LM transfer broadly; part of the 2018 pretraining wave GPT-2's lineage runs through GPT-1, not ELMo's biLSTM design.
candidate.definition: Representation model (Peters et al., 2018): deep contextualized word vectors from a bidirectional LSTM LM, improving six NLP benchmarks.
candidate.source_title: Deep contextualized word representations

candidate.name: BERT
candidate.lens: immediate prior state of the art
candidate.causal_claim: BERT is the encoder sibling of the 2018 pretraining wave - the alternative branch (masked, fine-tuned) to GPT-2's decoder, zero-shot branch; not consumed by GPT-2.
candidate.definition: Bidirectionally pretrained encoder (Devlin et al., 2018) whose fine-tuned representations reset NLP benchmarks.
candidate.source_title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding

candidate.name: Deep learning scaling predictability (Hestness)
candidate.causal_claim: Hestness et al. showed learning curves follow predictable power laws with scale - the empirical backdrop for GPT-2's log-linear scaling bet, though GPT-2's paper derives its claim from its own runs.
candidate.definition: Study (Hestness et al., 2017) demonstrating predictable power-law scaling of model performance with data and model size across applications.
candidate.source_title: Deep Learning Scaling is Predictable, Empirically

candidate.name: MAML meta-learning
candidate.causal_claim: MAML learns initializations for fast few-shot adaptation by gradient steps - the meta-learning paradigm GPT-2's conditioning-based few-shot bypassed entirely; no channel, as with ICL's expansion.
candidate.definition: Meta-learning algorithm (Finn, Abbeel & Levine, 2017) learning parameter initializations adaptable to new tasks in a few gradient steps.
candidate.source_title: Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning for Fast Adaptation of Deep Networks

candidate.name: Prototypical Networks
candidate.causal_claim: Prototypical Networks learn metric spaces for few-shot classification; part of the meta-learning paradigm with no channel into GPT-2's demonstration.
candidate.definition: Method (Snell, Swersky & Zemel, 2017) classifying by distance to class prototypes in a learned embedding space.
candidate.source_title: Prototypical Networks for Few-shot Learning

candidate.name: CoVe contextual vectors
candidate.lens: immediate prior state of the art
candidate.causal_claim: CoVe transferred MT-encoder representations to downstream tasks, an early transfer-representation result in the run-up to ELMo/GPT-1; its channel runs through that 2018 wave.
candidate.definition: Representations (McCann et al., 2017) from a machine-translation encoder, improving classification and QA when concatenated with GloVe.
candidate.source_title: Learned in Translation: Contextualized Word Vectors

candidate.name: AWD-LSTM
candidate.lens: immediate prior state of the art
candidate.causal_claim: AWD-LSTM was the strongest RNN LM recipe ULMFiT built on; it reaches GPT-2 through the ULMFiT/GPT-1 paradigm succession, as a SUBTYPE-relative of the LSTM line.
candidate.definition: Regularized LSTM LM (Merity, Keskar & Socher, 2017) whose recipe powered ULMFiT's transfer results.
candidate.source_title: Regularizing and Optimizing LSTM Language Models

candidate.name: Contextual pre-training via language modeling (Peters 2017 NAACL)
candidate.lens: immediate prior state of the art
candidate.causal_claim: The tagLM work preceding ELMo showed LM states helping sequence labelers; ancestry inside the ELMo branch of the 2018 wave.
candidate.definition: Work (Peters et al., 2017) augmenting sequence labelers with pretrained LM representations (tagLM), the direct run-up to ELMo.
candidate.source_title: Semi-supervised sequence tagging with bidirectional language models

candidate.name: CoQA
candidate.causal_claim: CoQA supplied GPT-2's flagship zero-shot number (55 F1 without task training); the stage for the demonstration, not an input to it.
candidate.definition: Conversational QA dataset (Reddy, Chen & Manning, 2018) of 127k questions over dialogues about passages, with rationale spans.
candidate.source_title: CoQA: A Conversational Question Answering Challenge

candidate.name: RACE reading comprehension
candidate.causal_claim: RACE was part of the reading-comprehension evaluation landscape GPT-2's zero-shot claims were situated in; not an input.
candidate.definition: Dataset (Lai et al., 2017) of 100k English-exam questions for middle/high school students, for reading comprehension.
candidate.source_title: RACE: Large-scale ReAding Comprehension Dataset From Examinations

candidate.name: GLUE benchmark
candidate.causal_claim: GLUE defined the fine-tuning era's scoreboard that GPT-2's zero-shot stance implicitly argued against; the incumbent measurement regime, not an enabler.
candidate.definition: Benchmark (Wang et al., 2018) of nine sentence-level understanding tasks that standardized transfer evaluation for BERT-era models.
candidate.source_title: GLUE: A Multi-Task Benchmark and Analysis Platform for Natural Language Understanding

candidate.name: ConvS2S
candidate.lens: immediate prior state of the art
candidate.causal_claim: Convolutional seq2seq was Facebook's parallel bet to the Transformer in 2017 - the sibling architecture line that lost; no channel into GPT-2.
candidate.definition: Architecture (Gehring et al., 2017) using gated convolutions with attention for sequence-to-sequence tasks, matching RNN quality faster.
candidate.source_title: Convolutional Sequence to Sequence Learning

candidate.name: Sparsely-Gated MoE
candidate.causal_claim: Shazeer's MoE scaled capacity via conditional computation - the road GPT-2 did not take (dense scaling); a sibling scaling philosophy with no channel.
candidate.definition: Architecture (Shazeer et al., 2017) inserting sparsely-gated mixture-of-experts layers to reach 137B parameters with conditional compute.
candidate.source_title: Outrageously Large Neural Networks: The Sparsely-Gated Mixture-of-Experts Layer

candidate.name: Relative position encodings
candidate.causal_claim: Shaw et al.'s relative positions improved Transformer self-attention; GPT-2 used learned absolute positions from the GPT-1 design, so the component channel does not reach it.
candidate.definition: Method (Shaw, Uszkoreit & Vaswani, 2018) representing relative positions in self-attention, improving translation quality.
candidate.source_title: Self-Attention with Relative Position Representations

candidate.name: Mixed-precision training
candidate.causal_claim: Mixed precision became standard large-training practice in this era; a generic technique GPT-2's run may have used but which no milestone claim attaches to.
candidate.definition: Technique (Micikevicius et al., 2017) training in FP16 with FP32 master weights, halving memory and speeding large runs.
candidate.source_title: Mixed Precision Training

candidate.name: AdamW and decoupled weight decay
candidate.causal_claim: AdamW fixed weight decay in adaptive optimizers; the GPT line's runs used Adam-family training generically - a sibling refinement, not a consumed milestone.
candidate.definition: Method (Loshchilov & Hutter, 2017) decoupling weight decay from gradient-based updates in Adam, improving generalization.
candidate.source_title: Decoupled Weight Decay Regularization

candidate.name: On the State of the Art of Evaluation in Neural Language Models
candidate.causal_claim: Melis et al. showed tuned LSTMs rivaling newer architectures - the evaluation-hygiene debate framing GPT-2's era; commentary, not a component.
candidate.definition: Study (Melis, Dyer & Blunsom, 2017) demonstrating standard LSTM LMs with tuned hyperparameters match or beat newer architectures.
candidate.source_title: On the State of the Art of Evaluation in Neural Language Models

candidate.name: MultiNLI
candidate.causal_claim: MultiNLI was a flagship transfer task of the GPT-1 fine-tuning demonstration; GPT-2's zero-shot stance bypassed the fine-tune eval regime it belongs to.
candidate.definition: Dataset (Williams, Nangia & Bowman, 2017) of 433k sentence pairs for natural language inference across genres.
candidate.source_title: A Broad-Coverage Challenge Corpus for Sentence Understanding through Inference

candidate.key_mechanism: A relation module scores query-support pairs instead of using a fixed distance.
candidate.name: Relation Networks
candidate.problem_solved: Learned the comparison metric itself for few-shot classification.

candidate.key_mechanism: A sequence model reads labeled examples and predicts for queries using attention to history.

candidate.problem_solved: Meta-learned with temporal convolutions and attention over past experience.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Strong few-shot results with a model-based meta-learner.

candidate.key_mechanism: Move the initialization toward weights obtained after training on a sampled task.

candidate.key_mechanism: A meta network produces fast weights for a base learner conditioned on support examples.
candidate.name: Meta Networks
candidate.problem_solved: Adapted rapidly by generating fast weights from task context.

candidate.key_mechanism: Context points are encoded and aggregated into a representation conditioning the decoder.
candidate.name: Conditional Neural Processes

candidate.scale_or_impact: Founded the neural-process family of conditional meta-learning.

candidate.key_mechanism: A Fisher-information penalty protects weights important to earlier tasks.
candidate.lineage: Continual-learning fix for the paradigm ICL sidesteps.
candidate.name: Elastic weight consolidation
candidate.problem_solved: Reduced catastrophic forgetting when learning sequential tasks.

candidate.key_mechanism: A shared leaderboard of sentence and sentence-pair tasks.
candidate.lineage: Measurement of the paradigm ICL displaced.
candidate.name: GLUE
candidate.problem_solved: Measured general language understanding across nine tasks in one benchmark.
candidate.scale_or_impact: The scoreboard of the fine-tune era.

candidate.key_mechanism: Transformer or deep-averaging encoders trained on multi-task data.
candidate.name: Universal Sentence Encoder
candidate.problem_solved: Provided off-the-shelf sentence embeddings for transfer tasks.

candidate.key_mechanism: Hebbian traces modulated by learned coefficients, trained by gradient descent.
candidate.name: Differentiable plasticity

raw_candidates.problem_solved: Learned from a single example by binding it to external memory in one shot.
raw_candidates.scale_or_impact: Model-based meta-learning milestone for one-shot tasks.

raw_candidates.key_mechanism: A meta network produces fast weights for a base learner conditioned on support examples.
raw_candidates.name: Meta Networks
raw_candidates.problem_solved: Adapted rapidly by generating fast weights from task context.
raw_candidates.scale_or_impact: Fast-weight meta-learning milestone.

raw_candidates.key_mechanism: Context points are encoded and aggregated into a representation conditioning the decoder.
raw_candidates.name: Conditional Neural Processes
raw_candidates.problem_solved: Predicted functions from a few context points in one forward pass.
raw_candidates.scale_or_impact: Founded the neural-process family of conditional meta-learning.

aliases: Human-level concept learning through probabilistic program induction
raw_candidates.key_mechanism: Probabilistic programs compose primitives into concepts, inferred by Bayesian sampling.
raw_candidates.name: Bayesian program learning
raw_candidates.problem_solved: Matched human one-shot concept learning on handwritten characters.
raw_candidates.scale_or_impact: Set the human-level one-shot benchmark (Omniglot).

raw_candidates.key_mechanism: A small hypernetwork outputs the weights of a larger main network.
raw_candidates.name: Hypernetworks
raw_candidates.problem_solved: Generated one network's weights with another network conditioned on context.
raw_candidates.scale_or_impact: Established weight-generation as a conditioning mechanism.

raw_candidates.key_mechanism: A Fisher-information penalty protects weights important to earlier tasks.
raw_candidates.lineage: Continual-learning fix for the paradigm ICL sidesteps.
raw_candidates.name: Elastic weight consolidation
raw_candidates.problem_solved: Reduced catastrophic forgetting when learning sequential tasks.
raw_candidates.scale_or_impact: Standard continual-learning baseline.

aliases: Google's Multilingual Neural Machine Translation System
raw_candidates.key_mechanism: A single NMT model with a target-language token transfers across pairs zero-shot.
raw_candidates.name: Multilingual zero-shot translation
raw_candidates.problem_solved: Translated between language pairs never seen together in training.
raw_candidates.scale_or_impact: First large-scale zero-shot transfer phenomenon in production NNs.

raw_candidates.key_mechanism: A shared leaderboard of sentence and sentence-pair tasks.
raw_candidates.lineage: Measurement of the paradigm ICL displaced.
raw_candidates.name: GLUE
raw_candidates.problem_solved: Measured general language understanding across nine tasks in one benchmark.
raw_candidates.scale_or_impact: The scoreboard of the fine-tune era.

raw_candidates.key_mechanism: Questions whose answers are spans in Wikipedia paragraphs, crowdsourced.
raw_candidates.name: SQuAD
raw_candidates.problem_solved: Gave reading comprehension a 100k-question benchmark.
raw_candidates.scale_or_impact: Drove the transfer-era QA race.

raw_candidates.key_mechanism: An encoder-decoder is trained to predict surrounding sentences.
raw_candidates.name: Skip-thought vectors
raw_candidates.problem_solved: Learned generic sentence representations without labels.
raw_candidates.scale_or_impact: Early unsupervised sentence-representation milestone.

raw_candidates.key_mechanism: Transformer or deep-averaging encoders trained on multi-task data.
raw_candidates.name: Universal Sentence Encoder
raw_candidates.problem_solved: Provided off-the-shelf sentence embeddings for transfer tasks.
raw_candidates.scale_or_impact: Widely used transfer embeddings.

raw_candidates.key_mechanism: Entropy and n-gram statistics measure the predictability of symbol sequences.
raw_candidates.name: Shannon information theory
raw_candidates.problem_solved: Quantified information and prediction, founding statistical language modeling.
raw_candidates.scale_or_impact: Foundation of information theory and LM evaluation.

raw_candidates.key_mechanism: Conditional probabilities over word histories with smoothing and backoff.
raw_candidates.name: N-gram language models
raw_candidates.problem_solved: Predicted words from fixed-order Markov statistics for speech recognition.
raw_candidates.scale_or_impact: Standard LM technology for three decades.

raw_candidates.key_mechanism: Hebbian traces modulated by learned coefficients, trained by gradient descent.
raw_candidates.name: Differentiable plasticity
raw_candidates.problem_solved: Learned per-connection plasticity rules for fast within-lifetime adaptation.
raw_candidates.scale_or_impact: Fast-adaptation mechanism research line.

raw_candidates.name: Luong attention (effective approaches to attention-based NMT)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: A refinement of Bahdanau attention; whatever it contributed to later attention practice arrived packaged in the Bahdanau attention mechanism it varies.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Luong, Pham & Manning, 2015): global and local attention variants for NMT, with input-feeding.
raw_candidates.source_title: Effective Approaches to Attention-based Neural Machine Translation

raw_candidates.name: ByteNet
raw_candidates.causal_claim: A parallel-computation rival to recurrence, but not an input to the Transformer's self-attention design.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture (Kalchbrenner et al., 2016): dilated-convolution encoder-decoder with linear-time decoding.
raw_candidates.source_title: ByteNet: A Convolutional Neural Network for Translation

raw_candidates.name: Google's neural machine translation system (GNMT)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The recurrent state of the art the Transformer displaced - context and rival, not a consumed enabler.
raw_candidates.definition: System (Wu et al., 2016): production LSTM encoder-decoder NMT with attention, deployed in Google Translate.
raw_candidates.source_title: Google's Neural Machine Translation System

raw_candidates.name: Decomposable attention model (Parikh et al.)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Shows attention-without-recurrence existed for NLI a year before the Transformer - a multiples data point, not a consumed channel into it.
raw_candidates.definition: Model (Parikh et al., 2016): attention-only natural-language-inference model with no recurrence, reaching top accuracy with far fewer parameters.
raw_candidates.source_title: A Decomposable Attention Model for Natural Language Inference

raw_candidates.name: ConvS2S (convolutional sequence to sequence)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Coeval with the Transformer (2017) - a parallel answer to the same problem, not a predecessor.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture (Gehring et al., 2017): fully convolutional encoder-decoder for translation.
raw_candidates.source_title: Convolutional Sequence to Sequence Learning

raw_candidates.name: Structured self-attentive sentence embedding (Lin et al.)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Coeval with the Transformer (2017); the term self-attention in print the same season, not a predecessor at year granularity.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Lin et al., 2017): self-attention over BiLSTM states for sentence embeddings.
raw_candidates.source_title: A Structured Self-attentive Sentence Embedding

raw_candidates.name: Scheduled sampling
raw_candidates.causal_claim: A training trick for recurrent decoders; not consumed by the Transformer's design.
raw_candidates.definition: Technique (Bengio et al., 2015): gradually feed model predictions instead of gold tokens during seq2seq training.
raw_candidates.source_title: Scheduled Sampling for Sequence Prediction with Recurrent Neural Networks

raw_candidates.name: Teacher forcing
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Generic recurrent-training machinery, superseded in relevance by the architecture change itself.
raw_candidates.definition: Technique (Williams & Zipser, 1989): train recurrent sequence models on gold previous outputs.
raw_candidates.source_title: A Learning Algorithm for Continually Running Fully Recurrent Neural Networks

raw_candidates.causal_claim: Kalchbrenner & Blunsom directly enabled the Transformer's leap by first posing machine translation as an end-to-end neural sequence problem - the problem formulation the Transformer answers in 2017.
raw_candidates.definition: Kalchbrenner & Blunsom's EMNLP 2013 model class: the first purely neural translation models, generating translations from continuous representations instead of discrete phrase tables.
raw_candidates.name: Recurrent continuous translation models (Kalchbrenner & Blunsom)
raw_candidates.source_title: Recurrent Continuous Translation Models (EMNLP 2013)

raw_candidates.causal_claim: Cho et al. directly enabled the Transformer's leap by posing the encoder-decoder formulation of neural translation - the template the Transformer re-architects with attention in place of recurrence.
raw_candidates.definition: Cho et al.'s EMNLP 2014 architecture: one RNN encodes a variable-length source into a fixed-length vector, a second RNN decodes the target; the paper also introduced the GRU cell.
raw_candidates.name: RNN Encoder-Decoder for statistical machine translation (Cho et al.)
raw_candidates.source_title: Learning Phrase Representations using RNN Encoder-Decoder for Statistical Machine Translation (EMNLP 2014)

raw_candidates.causal_claim: The WMT 2014 task directly enabled the Transformer's leap by posing the exact graded challenge - news translation on shared data with published numbers - on which the paper stakes its state-of-the-art claim.
raw_candidates.definition: The Ninth Workshop on Statistical Machine Translation's shared translation task (ACL 2014): common test sets, public training data, and published performance numbers for ten translation directions.
raw_candidates.name: WMT 2014 translation task
raw_candidates.source_title: Translation Task - ACL 2014 Ninth Workshop on Statistical Machine Translation

raw_candidates.causal_claim: Bengio, Simard & Frasconi directly enabled the Transformer's leap by first proving the obstruction - gradient flow through recurrence cannot carry long-range information - that the Transformer's removal of recurrence answers.
raw_candidates.definition: Bengio, Simard & Frasconi's 1994 IEEE TNN analysis proving the structural trade-off: a recurrent system that latches information robustly has gradients that vanish or explode exponentially over the same span.
raw_candidates.name: Learning long-term dependencies with gradient descent is difficult (Bengio, Simard & Frasconi)
raw_candidates.source_title: Learning long-term dependencies with gradient descent is difficult (IEEE Trans. Neural Networks, 1994)

raw_candidates.causal_claim: Pascanu, Mikolov & Bengio directly enabled the Transformer's leap by giving the definitive modern diagnosis of why recurrent training breaks - the pathology the attention-only design sidesteps entirely.
raw_candidates.definition: Pascanu, Mikolov & Bengio's ICML 2013 analysis of vanishing/exploding gradients from analytical, geometric, and dynamical-systems perspectives, building on Bengio et al. 1994; source of gradient-norm clipping.
raw_candidates.name: On the difficulty of training recurrent neural networks (Pascanu, Mikolov & Bengio)
raw_candidates.source_title: On the difficulty of training recurrent neural networks (ICML 2013)

raw_candidates.causal_claim: Hochreiter's 1991 analysis directly enabled the Transformer's leap by first naming the vanishing/exploding gradient obstruction in recurrent computation - the diagnosis the whole sequence-modeling lineage, Transformer included, designs against.
raw_candidates.definition: Hochreiter's 1991 diploma thesis: the first systematic analysis of vanishing and exploding gradients in recurrent networks, from which the LSTM design was later derived.
raw_candidates.name: Hochreiter's 1991 diploma thesis analysis of vanishing and exploding gradients (Untersuchungen zu dynamischen neuronalen Netzen)
raw_candidates.source_title: Hochreiter (1991), Untersuchungen zu dynamischen neuronalen Netzen (diploma thesis)

raw_candidates.causal_claim: Cho et al. directly enabled the Transformer's leap by measuring the obstruction - the fixed-length vector bottleneck degrading with sentence length - that attention, and then the Transformer, were designed against.
raw_candidates.definition: Cho, van Merrienboer & Bengio's SSST 2014 empirical study showing encoder-decoder translation quality degrades sharply as sentence length grows - the fixed-length bottleneck measured.
raw_candidates.name: On the properties of neural machine translation: encoder-decoder approaches (Cho et al.)
raw_candidates.source_title: On the Properties of Neural Machine Translation: Encoder-Decoder Approaches (SSST 2014)

raw_candidates.causal_claim: The WMT 2014 English-German corpus directly enabled the Transformer's leap by being the data the headline 28.4 BLEU result was trained and measured on.
raw_candidates.definition: The standard WMT 2014 English-German training set of about 4.5 million sentence pairs (Europarl, News Commentary, Common Crawl components), as used in the Transformer paper's section 5.1.
raw_candidates.name: WMT 2014 English-German parallel corpus
raw_candidates.source_title: Attention Is All You Need (arXiv:1706.03762)

raw_candidates.causal_claim: The WMT 2014 English-French corpus directly enabled the Transformer's leap by being the large-scale corpus on which the paper demonstrated the architecture scales to 36M sentence pairs.
raw_candidates.definition: The WMT 2014 English-French training set of 36 million sentences used for the Transformer's second headline result (41.0 BLEU single-model).
raw_candidates.name: WMT 2014 English-French parallel corpus
raw_candidates.source_title: Attention Is All You Need (arXiv:1706.03762)

raw_candidates.causal_claim: The P100 directly enabled the Transformer's leap by being the paper-documented training hardware: base model in 12 hours and big model in 3.5 days on a single 8-GPU machine - the training-cost fraction the leap is priced in.
raw_candidates.definition: NVIDIA's Pascal-generation datacenter accelerator (GP100, announced GTC April 2016): 16nm FinFET, HBM2 memory at 720 GB/s, NVLink interconnect; the Transformer paper (section 5.2) states all models were trained on one machine with 8 P100 GPUs.
raw_candidates.name: NVIDIA Tesla P100 GPU
raw_candidates.source_title: Inside Pascal: NVIDIA's Newest Computing Platform (NVIDIA Technical Blog, 2016)

raw_candidates.causal_claim: NVLink directly enabled the Transformer's leap by interconnecting the 8 P100s of the paper's single training machine at 160 GB/s, making single-node multi-GPU training of the big model practical.
raw_candidates.definition: NVIDIA's high-bandwidth GPU-to-GPU interconnect introduced with Pascal (160 GB/s bidirectional), interconnecting up to eight P100 GPUs in a single node.
raw_candidates.name: NVLink interconnect
raw_candidates.source_title: Inside Pascal: NVIDIA's Newest Computing Platform (NVIDIA Technical Blog, 2016)

raw_candidates.causal_claim: HBM2 directly enabled the Transformer's leap by feeding the P100s at 720 GB/s - the memory bandwidth the paper's 0.4-1.0 second training steps ran on.
raw_candidates.definition: Second-generation High Bandwidth Memory: stacked DRAM on a CoWoS package delivering 720 GB/s on the P100, 3x the bandwidth of the Maxwell generation.
raw_candidates.name: HBM2 high-bandwidth memory
raw_candidates.source_title: Inside Pascal: NVIDIA's Newest Computing Platform (NVIDIA Technical Blog, 2016)

raw_candidates.causal_claim: The TPU directly enabled the Transformer's leap by being Google's in-house accelerator fleet on which the architecture's training runs were executed inside Google.
raw_candidates.definition: Google's first-generation ASIC for neural-network inference, deployed in Google datacenters from 2015 and publicly announced at Google I/O in May 2016; inference-only, 92 TOPS integer.
raw_candidates.name: Google Tensor Processing Unit (TPU v1)
raw_candidates.source_title: Cloud TPU history (AI Wiki)

raw_candidates.causal_claim: CUDA directly enabled the Transformer's leap by being the programmability layer the P100 training hardware was actually programmed through - the specific software step between the silicon and the model code.
raw_candidates.definition: NVIDIA's parallel computing platform and programming model (2007) that made GPUs programmable for general computation - the layer through which TensorFlow kernels execute on the P100.
raw_candidates.name: CUDA GPU computing
raw_candidates.source_title: Inside Pascal: NVIDIA's Newest Computing Platform (NVIDIA Technical Blog, 2016)

raw_candidates.causal_claim: cuDNN directly enabled the Transformer's leap by supplying the tuned GPU kernels the model's TensorFlow training executed on the P100s.
raw_candidates.definition: NVIDIA's GPU-accelerated library of deep-neural-network primitives (2014): the convolution, activation, and normalization kernels frameworks like TensorFlow dispatch to on NVIDIA hardware.
raw_candidates.name: cuDNN
raw_candidates.source_title: Inside Pascal: NVIDIA's Newest Computing Platform (NVIDIA Technical Blog, 2016)

raw_candidates.causal_claim: Google Brain directly enabled the Transformer's leap by being the institutional vehicle - the team, the compute fleet, and the production NMT program - inside which all eight authors produced the paper in 2017.
raw_candidates.definition: Google's deep-learning research team, founded in 2011 by Andrew Ng, Jeff Dean, and Greg Corrado, combining open-ended ML research with Google-scale computing resources; the Transformer authors were Google Brain / Google Research staff.
raw_candidates.name: Google Brain
raw_candidates.source_title: Google Brain (Wikipedia)

raw_candidates.causal_claim: Production NMT at Google Translate directly enabled the Transformer's leap by creating, in late 2016, the demand condition the paper answers: its Table 2 prices the new architecture against GNMT in training cost.
raw_candidates.definition: The production rollout of GNMT: Chinese-English went live 27 Sept 2016 and eight language pairs on 15 Nov 2016, putting neural translation in front of Google Translate's full user base and making NMT training/inference cost a production quantity.
raw_candidates.name: Neural machine translation in production at Google Translate
raw_candidates.source_title: Found in translation: More accurate, fluent sentences in Google Translate (Google Blog, Nov 15 2016)

raw_candidates.causal_claim: The TensorFlow 1.0 release directly enabled the Transformer's leap by stabilizing, in February 2017, the framework API the paper's implementation was built and released against.
raw_candidates.definition: TensorFlow's first stable release (15 Feb 2017), promising Python API stability and shipping the XLA compiler groundwork - the framework reaching production maturity months before the Transformer paper.
raw_candidates.name: TensorFlow 1.0 release
raw_candidates.source_title: Announcing TensorFlow 1.0 (Google Developers Blog, Feb 15 2017)

raw_candidates.causal_claim: AlphaGo's victory directly enabled the Transformer's leap by establishing, inside Google in 2016, the organizational proof that large-scale neural systems win - the climate in which an all-attention architecture bet was funded and staffed.
raw_candidates.definition: DeepMind's AlphaGo defeated Lee Sedol 4-1 in March 2016, powered by TPUs - the public demonstration, one year before the Transformer, that datacenter-scale neural computation was Google's strategic direction.
raw_candidates.name: AlphaGo's victory over Lee Sedol
raw_candidates.source_title: TPU Chip (AI Wiki)

candidate.name: Transformer architecture
candidate.causal_claim: GPT-2 is a stack of Transformer decoder blocks; the architecture reaches it as part of the GPT-1 recipe it inherited and scaled.
candidate.definition: Architecture (Vaswani et al., 2017) replacing recurrence with self-attention; the substrate of all modern LLMs.
candidate.source_title: Attention Is All You Need

candidate.name: ULMFiT
candidate.lens: immediate prior state of the art
candidate.causal_claim: ULMFiT proved pretrain-then-fine-tune for NLP months before GPT-1, defining the transfer paradigm GPT-2's zero-shot move reacted against and extended.
candidate.definition: Method (Howard & Ruder, 2018): LM pretraining, LM fine-tuning, classifier fine-tuning with discriminative rates and gradual unfreezing, large gains on text classification.
candidate.source_title: Universal Language Model Fine-tuning for Text Classification

candidate.name: ELMo
candidate.lens: immediate prior state of the art
candidate.causal_claim: ELMo showed contextualized representations from a pretrained LM transfer broadly; part of the 2018 pretraining wave GPT-2's lineage runs through GPT-1, not ELMo's biLSTM design.
candidate.definition: Representation model (Peters et al., 2018): deep contextualized word vectors from a bidirectional LSTM LM, improving six NLP benchmarks.
candidate.source_title: Deep contextualized word representations

candidate.name: BERT
candidate.lens: immediate prior state of the art
candidate.causal_claim: BERT is the encoder sibling of the 2018 pretraining wave - the alternative branch (masked, fine-tuned) to GPT-2's decoder, zero-shot branch; not consumed by GPT-2.
candidate.definition: Bidirectionally pretrained encoder (Devlin et al., 2018) whose fine-tuned representations reset NLP benchmarks.
candidate.source_title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding

candidate.name: Deep learning scaling predictability (Hestness)
candidate.causal_claim: Hestness et al. showed learning curves follow predictable power laws with scale - the empirical backdrop for GPT-2's log-linear scaling bet, though GPT-2's paper derives its claim from its own runs.
candidate.definition: Study (Hestness et al., 2017) demonstrating predictable power-law scaling of model performance with data and model size across applications.
candidate.source_title: Deep Learning Scaling is Predictable, Empirically

candidate.name: MAML meta-learning
candidate.causal_claim: MAML learns initializations for fast few-shot adaptation by gradient steps - the meta-learning paradigm GPT-2's conditioning-based few-shot bypassed entirely; no channel, as with ICL's expansion.
candidate.definition: Meta-learning algorithm (Finn, Abbeel & Levine, 2017) learning parameter initializations adaptable to new tasks in a few gradient steps.
candidate.source_title: Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning for Fast Adaptation of Deep Networks

candidate.name: Prototypical Networks
candidate.causal_claim: Prototypical Networks learn metric spaces for few-shot classification; part of the meta-learning paradigm with no channel into GPT-2's demonstration.
candidate.definition: Method (Snell, Swersky & Zemel, 2017) classifying by distance to class prototypes in a learned embedding space.
candidate.source_title: Prototypical Networks for Few-shot Learning

candidate.name: CoVe contextual vectors
candidate.lens: immediate prior state of the art
candidate.causal_claim: CoVe transferred MT-encoder representations to downstream tasks, an early transfer-representation result in the run-up to ELMo/GPT-1; its channel runs through that 2018 wave.
candidate.definition: Representations (McCann et al., 2017) from a machine-translation encoder, improving classification and QA when concatenated with GloVe.
candidate.source_title: Learned in Translation: Contextualized Word Vectors

candidate.name: AWD-LSTM
candidate.lens: immediate prior state of the art
candidate.causal_claim: AWD-LSTM was the strongest RNN LM recipe ULMFiT built on; it reaches GPT-2 through the ULMFiT/GPT-1 paradigm succession, as a SUBTYPE-relative of the LSTM line.
candidate.definition: Regularized LSTM LM (Merity, Keskar & Socher, 2017) whose recipe powered ULMFiT's transfer results.
candidate.source_title: Regularizing and Optimizing LSTM Language Models

candidate.name: Contextual pre-training via language modeling (Peters 2017 NAACL)
candidate.lens: immediate prior state of the art
candidate.causal_claim: The tagLM work preceding ELMo showed LM states helping sequence labelers; ancestry inside the ELMo branch of the 2018 wave.
candidate.definition: Work (Peters et al., 2017) augmenting sequence labelers with pretrained LM representations (tagLM), the direct run-up to ELMo.
candidate.source_title: Semi-supervised sequence tagging with bidirectional language models

candidate.name: CoQA
candidate.causal_claim: CoQA supplied GPT-2's flagship zero-shot number (55 F1 without task training); the stage for the demonstration, not an input to it.
candidate.definition: Conversational QA dataset (Reddy, Chen & Manning, 2018) of 127k questions over dialogues about passages, with rationale spans.
candidate.source_title: CoQA: A Conversational Question Answering Challenge

candidate.name: RACE reading comprehension
candidate.causal_claim: RACE was part of the reading-comprehension evaluation landscape GPT-2's zero-shot claims were situated in; not an input.
candidate.definition: Dataset (Lai et al., 2017) of 100k English-exam questions for middle/high school students, for reading comprehension.
candidate.source_title: RACE: Large-scale ReAding Comprehension Dataset From Examinations

candidate.name: GLUE benchmark
candidate.causal_claim: GLUE defined the fine-tuning era's scoreboard that GPT-2's zero-shot stance implicitly argued against; the incumbent measurement regime, not an enabler.
candidate.definition: Benchmark (Wang et al., 2018) of nine sentence-level understanding tasks that standardized transfer evaluation for BERT-era models.
candidate.source_title: GLUE: A Multi-Task Benchmark and Analysis Platform for Natural Language Understanding

candidate.name: ConvS2S
candidate.lens: immediate prior state of the art
candidate.causal_claim: Convolutional seq2seq was Facebook's parallel bet to the Transformer in 2017 - the sibling architecture line that lost; no channel into GPT-2.
candidate.definition: Architecture (Gehring et al., 2017) using gated convolutions with attention for sequence-to-sequence tasks, matching RNN quality faster.
candidate.source_title: Convolutional Sequence to Sequence Learning

candidate.name: Sparsely-Gated MoE
candidate.causal_claim: Shazeer's MoE scaled capacity via conditional computation - the road GPT-2 did not take (dense scaling); a sibling scaling philosophy with no channel.
candidate.definition: Architecture (Shazeer et al., 2017) inserting sparsely-gated mixture-of-experts layers to reach 137B parameters with conditional compute.
candidate.source_title: Outrageously Large Neural Networks: The Sparsely-Gated Mixture-of-Experts Layer

candidate.name: Relative position encodings
candidate.causal_claim: Shaw et al.'s relative positions improved Transformer self-attention; GPT-2 used learned absolute positions from the GPT-1 design, so the component channel does not reach it.
candidate.definition: Method (Shaw, Uszkoreit & Vaswani, 2018) representing relative positions in self-attention, improving translation quality.
candidate.source_title: Self-Attention with Relative Position Representations

candidate.name: Mixed-precision training
candidate.causal_claim: Mixed precision became standard large-training practice in this era; a generic technique GPT-2's run may have used but which no milestone claim attaches to.
candidate.definition: Technique (Micikevicius et al., 2017) training in FP16 with FP32 master weights, halving memory and speeding large runs.
candidate.source_title: Mixed Precision Training

candidate.name: AdamW and decoupled weight decay
candidate.causal_claim: AdamW fixed weight decay in adaptive optimizers; the GPT line's runs used Adam-family training generically - a sibling refinement, not a consumed milestone.
candidate.definition: Method (Loshchilov & Hutter, 2017) decoupling weight decay from gradient-based updates in Adam, improving generalization.
candidate.source_title: Decoupled Weight Decay Regularization

candidate.name: On the State of the Art of Evaluation in Neural Language Models
candidate.causal_claim: Melis et al. showed tuned LSTMs rivaling newer architectures - the evaluation-hygiene debate framing GPT-2's era; commentary, not a component.
candidate.definition: Study (Melis, Dyer & Blunsom, 2017) demonstrating standard LSTM LMs with tuned hyperparameters match or beat newer architectures.
candidate.source_title: On the State of the Art of Evaluation in Neural Language Models

candidate.name: MultiNLI
candidate.causal_claim: MultiNLI was a flagship transfer task of the GPT-1 fine-tuning demonstration; GPT-2's zero-shot stance bypassed the fine-tune eval regime it belongs to.
candidate.definition: Dataset (Williams, Nangia & Bowman, 2017) of 433k sentence pairs for natural language inference across genres.
candidate.source_title: A Broad-Coverage Challenge Corpus for Sentence Understanding through Inference

candidate.key_mechanism: A relation module scores query-support pairs instead of using a fixed distance.
candidate.name: Relation Networks
candidate.problem_solved: Learned the comparison metric itself for few-shot classification.

candidate.key_mechanism: A sequence model reads labeled examples and predicts for queries using attention to history.
candidate.name: SNAIL
candidate.problem_solved: Meta-learned with temporal convolutions and attention over past experience.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Strong few-shot results with a model-based meta-learner.

candidate.key_mechanism: Move the initialization toward weights obtained after training on a sampled task.
candidate.name: Reptile
candidate.problem_solved: Simplified first-order meta-learning for fast adaptation.

aliases: Optimization as a Model for Few-Shot Learning
candidate.key_mechanism: An LSTM meta-learner ingests gradients and updates the learner's parameters cell-state style.
candidate.name: LSTM meta-learner
candidate.problem_solved: Learned an optimizer that adapts a learner to few-shot tasks.

candidate.key_mechanism: A meta network produces fast weights for a base learner conditioned on support examples.
candidate.name: Meta Networks
candidate.problem_solved: Adapted rapidly by generating fast weights from task context.

candidate.key_mechanism: Context points are encoded and aggregated into a representation conditioning the decoder.
candidate.name: Conditional Neural Processes
candidate.problem_solved: Predicted functions from a few context points in one forward pass.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Founded the neural-process family of conditional meta-learning.

candidate.key_mechanism: A Fisher-information penalty protects weights important to earlier tasks.
candidate.lineage: Continual-learning fix for the paradigm ICL sidesteps.
candidate.name: Elastic weight consolidation
candidate.problem_solved: Reduced catastrophic forgetting when learning sequential tasks.

candidate.key_mechanism: A shared leaderboard of sentence and sentence-pair tasks.
candidate.lineage: Measurement of the paradigm ICL displaced.
candidate.name: GLUE
candidate.problem_solved: Measured general language understanding across nine tasks in one benchmark.
candidate.scale_or_impact: The scoreboard of the fine-tune era.

candidate.key_mechanism: Transformer or deep-averaging encoders trained on multi-task data.
candidate.name: Universal Sentence Encoder
candidate.problem_solved: Provided off-the-shelf sentence embeddings for transfer tasks.

candidate.key_mechanism: Hebbian traces modulated by learned coefficients, trained by gradient descent.
candidate.name: Differentiable plasticity
candidate.problem_solved: Learned per-connection plasticity rules for fast within-lifetime adaptation.

candidate.name: ConvS2S (convolutional sequence to sequence)
candidate.causal_claim: Coeval with the Transformer (2017) - a parallel answer to the same problem, not a predecessor.
candidate.definition: Architecture (Gehring et al., 2017): fully convolutional encoder-decoder for translation.
candidate.source_title: Convolutional Sequence to Sequence Learning

candidate.name: Structured self-attentive sentence embedding (Lin et al.)
candidate.causal_claim: Coeval with the Transformer (2017); the term self-attention in print the same season, not a predecessor at year granularity.
candidate.definition: Method (Lin et al., 2017): self-attention over BiLSTM states for sentence embeddings.
candidate.source_title: A Structured Self-attentive Sentence Embedding

candidate.causal_claim: The TensorFlow 1.0 release directly enabled the Transformer's leap by stabilizing, in February 2017, the framework API the paper's implementation was built and released against.
candidate.definition: TensorFlow's first stable release (15 Feb 2017), promising Python API stability and shipping the XLA compiler groundwork - the framework reaching production maturity months before the Transformer paper.
candidate.name: TensorFlow 1.0 release
candidate.source_title: Announcing TensorFlow 1.0 (Google Developers Blog, Feb 15 2017)

raw_candidates.name: Generative pretraining (GPT-1)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: GPT-1 is GPT-2's literal predecessor in the same lab: the Transformer-decoder generative-pretraining recipe GPT-2 scaled 10x and pushed from fine-tuning to zero-shot conditioning.
raw_candidates.definition: OpenAI model (Radford et al., 2018): a 117M Transformer decoder pretrained on BooksCorpus, then fine-tuned per task, beating purpose-built models on 9 of 12 language-understanding tasks.
raw_candidates.source_title: Improving Language Understanding by Generative Pre-Training

raw_candidates.name: Transformer architecture
raw_candidates.causal_claim: GPT-2 is a stack of Transformer decoder blocks; the architecture reaches it as part of the GPT-1 recipe it inherited and scaled.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture (Vaswani et al., 2017) replacing recurrence with self-attention; the substrate of all modern LLMs.
raw_candidates.source_title: Attention Is All You Need

raw_candidates.name: ULMFiT
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: ULMFiT proved pretrain-then-fine-tune for NLP months before GPT-1, defining the transfer paradigm GPT-2's zero-shot move reacted against and extended.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Howard & Ruder, 2018): LM pretraining, LM fine-tuning, classifier fine-tuning with discriminative rates and gradual unfreezing, large gains on text classification.
raw_candidates.source_title: Universal Language Model Fine-tuning for Text Classification

raw_candidates.name: ELMo
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: ELMo showed contextualized representations from a pretrained LM transfer broadly; part of the 2018 pretraining wave GPT-2's lineage runs through GPT-1, not ELMo's biLSTM design.
raw_candidates.definition: Representation model (Peters et al., 2018): deep contextualized word vectors from a bidirectional LSTM LM, improving six NLP benchmarks.
raw_candidates.source_title: Deep contextualized word representations

raw_candidates.name: BERT
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: BERT is the encoder sibling of the 2018 pretraining wave - the alternative branch (masked, fine-tuned) to GPT-2's decoder, zero-shot branch; not consumed by GPT-2.
raw_candidates.definition: Bidirectionally pretrained encoder (Devlin et al., 2018) whose fine-tuned representations reset NLP benchmarks.
raw_candidates.source_title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding

raw_candidates.name: Neural probabilistic language model
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Bengio's NPLM founded neural language modeling - distributed word representations learned jointly with the LM; the deep ancestor of the pretraining lineage, reaching GPT-2 through GPT-1 and the Transformer succession.
raw_candidates.definition: Model (Bengio et al., 2003) learning distributed word embeddings jointly with a neural LM, beating n-gram models on perplexity.
raw_candidates.source_title: A Neural Probabilistic Language Model

raw_candidates.name: Word2vec
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Word2vec industrialized learned embeddings, the representation premise pretraining scaled; it reaches GPT-2 through the whole pretraining tradition.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Mikolov et al., 2013) learning word embeddings from co-occurrence prediction at scale.
raw_candidates.source_title: Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space

raw_candidates.name: RNN language modeling (Mikolov)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Mikolov's RNNLM showed neural LMs decisively beating n-gram baselines, restarting LM research as a neural discipline; an ancestor at several removes.
raw_candidates.definition: Recurrent neural LM (Mikolov et al., 2010) reducing perplexity and WER substantially over backoff n-gram models.
raw_candidates.source_title: Recurrent neural network based language model

raw_candidates.name: Byte-pair encoding for NMT
raw_candidates.causal_claim: BPE subword segmentation is GPT-2's tokenization family (byte-level BPE); the segmentation scheme was inherited as part of the GPT-1 recipe and tooling.
raw_candidates.definition: Segmentation method (Sennrich et al., 2016) applying byte-pair encoding to learn subword units, fixing rare-word handling in neural MT.
raw_candidates.source_title: Neural Machine Translation of Rare Words with Subword Units

raw_candidates.name: Layer normalization
raw_candidates.causal_claim: LayerNorm stabilizes the Transformer blocks GPT-2 stacks (moved to pre-norm in GPT-2); it arrives inside the inherited GPT-1 architecture, not as a separately consumed result.
raw_candidates.definition: Normalization method (Ba, Kiros & Hinton, 2016) normalizing layer activations per example, stabilizing recurrent and deep training.
raw_candidates.source_title: Layer Normalization

raw_candidates.name: Adam optimizer
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Adam is the optimizer family the GPT line trained with; a commodity component of the inherited training recipe, not a GPT-2-specific enabler.
raw_candidates.definition: Optimizer (Kingma & Ba, 2014) with adaptive per-parameter rates from first/second moment estimates; became deep learning's default.
raw_candidates.source_title: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization

raw_candidates.name: GELU activation
raw_candidates.causal_claim: GELU is the activation the GPT line adopted from GPT-1 onward; it reaches GPT-2 inside the inherited architecture.
raw_candidates.definition: Activation (Hendrycks & Gimpel, 2016) weighting inputs by their Gaussian CDF, adopted across Transformer models.
raw_candidates.source_title: Gaussian Error Linear Units (GELUs)

raw_candidates.name: BooksCorpus
raw_candidates.causal_claim: BooksCorpus was GPT-1's pretraining corpus - the data half of the recipe GPT-2 replaced with WebText; its channel runs through GPT-1.
raw_candidates.definition: Dataset (Zhu et al., 2015) of 11,038 unpublished books (~74M sentences) used to train the original GPT.
raw_candidates.source_title: Aligning Books and Movies: Towards Story-like Visual Explanations by Watching Movies and Reading Books

raw_candidates.name: Common Crawl
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Common Crawl is the web-scale corpus infrastructure of the era; GPT-2's WebText was deliberately NOT Common Crawl (Reddit-linked pages instead), so the channel is weak.
raw_candidates.definition: Nonprofit web archive (founded 2007-08) providing petabytes of crawled web pages used to train many LMs.
raw_candidates.source_title: Common Crawl

raw_candidates.name: Deep learning scaling predictability (Hestness)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Hestness et al. showed learning curves follow predictable power laws with scale - the empirical backdrop for GPT-2's log-linear scaling bet, though GPT-2's paper derives its claim from its own runs.
raw_candidates.definition: Study (Hestness et al., 2017) demonstrating predictable power-law scaling of model performance with data and model size across applications.
raw_candidates.source_title: Deep Learning Scaling is Predictable, Empirically

raw_candidates.name: AlexNet
raw_candidates.causal_claim: AlexNet opened the deep-learning era whose scaling logic GPT-2 extends to language; it reaches GPT-2 through the entire deep-learning succession, not directly.
raw_candidates.definition: CNN (Krizhevsky, Sutskever & Hinton, 2012) winning ImageNet by a wide margin with GPU training, founding the deep-learning era.
raw_candidates.source_title: ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks

raw_candidates.name: CUDA GPU computing
raw_candidates.causal_claim: CUDA made the GPU training of every model in this lineage practical; it reaches GPT-2 as inherited infrastructure, two successions removed.
raw_candidates.definition: Platform (NVIDIA, 2007) exposing GPU parallelism to general computation, the substrate of deep-learning training economics.
raw_candidates.source_title: CUDA

raw_candidates.name: Backpropagation
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Backpropagation trained every network in the lineage; it reaches GPT-2 through the models and recipes that embody it.
raw_candidates.definition: Algorithm (Rumelhart, Hinton & Williams, 1986) computing gradients through layered networks by the chain rule.
raw_candidates.source_title: Backpropagation

raw_candidates.name: LSTM
raw_candidates.causal_claim: LSTMs were the pre-Transformer LM substrate (ELMo, ULMFiT); GPT-2's lineage displaced them via the Transformer, which is the channel.
raw_candidates.definition: Recurrent architecture (Hochreiter & Schmidhuber, 1997) with gated memory cells for long-range sequence learning.
raw_candidates.source_title: Long short-term memory

raw_candidates.name: Sequence-to-sequence learning
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Seq2seq founded neural sequence transduction; it reaches GPT-2 through the Transformer that displaced it.
raw_candidates.definition: Framework (Sutskever et al., 2014) mapping sequences to sequences with LSTM encoder-decoders.
raw_candidates.source_title: Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks

raw_candidates.name: Bahdanau attention
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Bahdanau attention is the Transformer's own predecessor; it reaches GPT-2 inside self-attention, via the Transformer.
raw_candidates.definition: Mechanism (Bahdanau et al., 2014) letting a decoder attend over encoder states in neural MT.
raw_candidates.source_title: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate

raw_candidates.name: MAML meta-learning
raw_candidates.causal_claim: MAML learns initializations for fast few-shot adaptation by gradient steps - the meta-learning paradigm GPT-2's conditioning-based few-shot bypassed entirely; no channel, as with ICL's expansion.
raw_candidates.definition: Meta-learning algorithm (Finn, Abbeel & Levine, 2017) learning parameter initializations adaptable to new tasks in a few gradient steps.
raw_candidates.source_title: Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning for Fast Adaptation of Deep Networks

raw_candidates.name: Matching Networks
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Matching Networks did one-shot classification by attention over support examples - a conditioning-flavored few-shot method, but embedding-based and never consumed by the GPT line.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture (Vinyals et al., 2016) for one-shot learning via attention over a support set in embedding space.
raw_candidates.source_title: Matching Networks for One Shot Learning

raw_candidates.name: Prototypical Networks
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Prototypical Networks learn metric spaces for few-shot classification; part of the meta-learning paradigm with no channel into GPT-2's demonstration.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Snell, Swersky & Zemel, 2017) classifying by distance to class prototypes in a learned embedding space.
raw_candidates.source_title: Prototypical Networks for Few-shot Learning

raw_candidates.name: Zero-shot learning via attributes
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Attribute-based zero-shot classification in vision showed category transfer without examples a decade earlier - a conceptual sibling in another modality, with no channel into GPT-2.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Lampert, Nickisch & Harmeling, 2009) classifying unseen animal classes via human-specified attribute vectors.
raw_candidates.source_title: Learning to detect unseen object classes by between-class attribute transfer

raw_candidates.name: Kneser-Ney smoothing
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Kneser-Ney was the statistical-LM state of the art the neural lineage displaced; ancestry of the task, not of the method.
raw_candidates.definition: Smoothing technique (Kneser & Ney, 1995) for n-gram LMs, the best-performing backoff scheme of the statistical era.
raw_candidates.source_title: Kneser-Ney smoothing

raw_candidates.name: Perplexity as LM metric
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Perplexity (Jelinek-era) is the yardstick GPT-2's log-linear scaling claim is stated in; a measurement convention, not an enabler of the capability.
raw_candidates.definition: Metric from speech-recognition LM evaluation (Jelinek, 1970s): exponentiated cross-entropy of a test set under the model.
raw_candidates.source_title: Perplexity

raw_candidates.name: One Billion Word Benchmark
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The 1B Word Benchmark standardized neural LM comparison in the pre-Transformer years; part of the evaluation lineage, not an input to GPT-2.
raw_candidates.definition: Benchmark (Chelba et al., 2013) for statistical language modeling at billion-word scale.
raw_candidates.source_title: One Billion Word Benchmark for Measuring Progress in Statistical Language Modeling

raw_candidates.name: Penn Treebank LM benchmark
raw_candidates.causal_claim: PTB was the small-data LM testbed of the neural-LM era (Mikolov's RNNLM results); evaluation ancestry only.
raw_candidates.definition: Corpus (Marcus et al., 1993) whose LM split became the standard small benchmark for neural language models.
raw_candidates.source_title: Penn Treebank

raw_candidates.name: TensorFlow
raw_candidates.causal_claim: GPT-1/GPT-2 were implemented in TensorFlow; commodity tooling any equivalent framework replaces, not a milestone in the method's causal chain.
raw_candidates.definition: Google's open-source deep-learning framework (2015) for dataflow graph computation.
raw_candidates.source_title: TensorFlow

raw_candidates.name: PyTorch
raw_candidates.causal_claim: PyTorch was the era's other framework; the GPT line's public code was TensorFlow-based, so even the tooling channel points elsewhere.
raw_candidates.definition: Facebook's open-source deep-learning framework (2016) with dynamic computation graphs.
raw_candidates.source_title: PyTorch

raw_candidates.name: Distributed training (parameter servers)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Large-scale distributed training patterns underpin all big-model runs of the era; GPT-2's 1.5B training was modest by later standards and consumed no specific distributed-training milestone.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture pattern (Li et al., 2014) scaling ML training across clusters via parameter servers.
raw_candidates.source_title: Scaling Distributed Machine Learning with the Parameter Server

raw_candidates.name: Curriculum learning
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Curriculum learning orders training examples easy-to-hard; GPT-2's training used no curriculum - a named idea in the training-methods space with no channel.
raw_candidates.definition: Strategy (Bengio et al., 2009) presenting training examples in a meaningful order to improve generalization and speed.
raw_candidates.source_title: Curriculum Learning

raw_candidates.name: Generating sequences with RNNs (Graves)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Graves 2013 showed RNNs generating convincing text and handwriting sample-by-sample - the generative-LM demonstration tradition GPT-2 scales; ancestry through the neural-LM lineage.
raw_candidates.definition: Work (Graves, 2013) using LSTMs with mixture-density outputs to generate handwriting and text sequences.
raw_candidates.source_title: Generating Sequences With Recurrent Neural Networks

raw_candidates.name: CoVe contextual vectors
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: CoVe transferred MT-encoder representations to downstream tasks, an early transfer-representation result in the run-up to ELMo/GPT-1; its channel runs through that 2018 wave.
raw_candidates.definition: Representations (McCann et al., 2017) from a machine-translation encoder, improving classification and QA when concatenated with GloVe.
raw_candidates.source_title: Learned in Translation: Contextualized Word Vectors

raw_candidates.name: GloVe
raw_candidates.causal_claim: GloVe was the other embedding standard of the word2vec era; the embedding premise reaches GPT-2 through the pretraining tradition, and GPT-2 learns its embeddings end-to-end regardless.
raw_candidates.definition: Embedding method (Pennington, Socher & Manning, 2014) factorizing global co-occurrence statistics.
raw_candidates.source_title: GloVe: Global Vectors for Word Representation

raw_candidates.name: Fast weights (Schmidhuber)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Schmidhuber's fast-weight programmers proposed one network programming another via weight changes - a conceptual ancestor of conditioning, cited by later meta-learning, with no channel into GPT-2's work.
raw_candidates.definition: Proposal (Schmidhuber, 1992) in which a slow network generates fast weights for another network, an early form of learned adaptation.
raw_candidates.source_title: Learning to Control Fast-Weight Memories: An Alternative to Dynamic Recurrent Networks

raw_candidates.name: Learning to learn (Thrun & Pratt)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The learning-to-learn literature framed transfer as meta-knowledge decades before; framing ancestry for few-shot claims, not a consumed component.
raw_candidates.definition: Research programme (Thrun & Pratt, eds., 1998) on learning inductive bias from task families.
raw_candidates.source_title: Learning to Learn

raw_candidates.name: Neural Turing Machines
raw_candidates.causal_claim: NTMs coupled networks to external memory; an alternative augmentation direction that the GPT lineage did not take.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture (Graves et al., 2014) giving a neural controller differentiable read/write access to an external memory bank.
raw_candidates.source_title: Neural Turing Machines

raw_candidates.name: Memory Networks
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Memory Networks answered questions over an explicit memory store; a sibling QA architecture with no channel into GPT-2.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture (Weston, Chopra & Bordes, 2014) combining learned representations with a long-term memory component for QA.
raw_candidates.source_title: Memory Networks

raw_candidates.name: End-to-End Memory Networks
raw_candidates.causal_claim: MemN2N made memory attention end-to-end differentiable; part of the attention-era QA landscape, not GPT-2's lineage.
raw_candidates.definition: Model (Sukhbaatar et al., 2015) reading memory with multiple attention hops, trained end-to-end.
raw_candidates.source_title: End-To-End Memory Networks

raw_candidates.name: Differentiable Neural Computer
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The DNC was DeepMind's flagship memory-augmented architecture; a parallel direction with no channel into the GPT line.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture (Graves et al., 2016) coupling a neural controller to an external memory matrix with differentiable addressing.
raw_candidates.source_title: Hybrid computing using a neural network with dynamic external memory

raw_candidates.name: Transformer-XL
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Transformer-XL extended context via recurrence in Jan 2019 - coeval with GPT-2 (same year), listed to be dropped by the year bound.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture (Dai et al., 2019) adding segment-level recurrence and relative positions to the Transformer for longer contexts.
raw_candidates.source_title: Transformer-XL: Attentive Language Models Beyond a Fixed-Length Context

raw_candidates.name: XLNet
raw_candidates.causal_claim: XLNet's permutation LM was 2019's alternative pretraining objective - coeval with GPT-2, dropped by the year bound.
raw_candidates.definition: Pretraining method (Yang et al., 2019) maximizing likelihood over permutation orders, combining autoregressive and autoencoding advantages.
raw_candidates.source_title: XLNet: Generalized Autoregressive Pretraining for Language Understanding

raw_candidates.name: RoBERTa
raw_candidates.causal_claim: RoBERTa showed BERT was undertrained - a coeval 2019 replication study, dropped by the year bound.
raw_candidates.definition: Study (Liu et al., 2019) optimizing BERT's training recipe for substantially better results.
raw_candidates.source_title: RoBERTa: A Robustly Optimized BERT Pretraining Approach

raw_candidates.name: ERNIE
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Baidu's ERNIE added knowledge masking to pretraining in 2019 - coeval, dropped by the year bound.
raw_candidates.definition: Pretraining model (Sun et al., 2019) masking entities and phrases to inject knowledge into representations.
raw_candidates.source_title: ERNIE: Enhanced Representation through Knowledge Integration

raw_candidates.name: GPT-2 staged release and 'too dangerous to release' debate
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The staged-release controversy is part of GPT-2's own 2019 story, not a predecessor - coeval, dropped by the year bound.
raw_candidates.definition: OpenAI's staged release of GPT-2 (Feb-Nov 2019) over misuse concerns, a landmark in release-policy debates.
raw_candidates.source_title: GPT-2

raw_candidates.name: Residual networks (ResNet)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Residual connections are inside every Transformer block GPT-2 stacks; they arrive as part of the Transformer/GPT-1 architecture, not as a separately consumed result.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture (He et al., 2015) with skip connections enabling training of 100+ layer networks, winning ImageNet 2015.
raw_candidates.source_title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition

raw_candidates.name: Dropout
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Dropout is a standard regularizer inside the inherited training recipe; commodity component, not a GPT-2 enabler in the milestone sense.
raw_candidates.definition: Regularization technique (Srivastava et al., 2014) randomly dropping units during training to prevent co-adaptation.
raw_candidates.source_title: Dropout: A Simple Way to Prevent Neural Networks from Overfitting

raw_candidates.name: Batch normalization
raw_candidates.causal_claim: BatchNorm normalized activations across batches; the Transformer line standardized on LayerNorm instead, so even the component channel points to its sibling.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Ioffe & Szegedy, 2015) normalizing layer inputs per mini-batch, accelerating deep training.
raw_candidates.source_title: Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training by Reducing Internal Covariate Shift

raw_candidates.name: Weight initialization (Xavier/He)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Principled initialization is inside every training run of the era; background technique, not a milestone GPT-2 distinctively consumed (GPT-2's scaled residual init is its own tweak).
raw_candidates.definition: Initialization schemes (Glorot & Bengio, 2010; He et al., 2015) keeping activation/gradient scales stable across layers.
raw_candidates.source_title: Understanding the difficulty of training deep feedforward neural networks

raw_candidates.name: Stochastic gradient descent with momentum
